sections.title: Basic Concept of Homonyms and Confusing Words
sections.content: Homonyms or homophones are words that sound the same but have different meanings and spellings. In competitive exams, a sentence context is usually given to help choose the correct word.

sections.title: Homophones (Same Sound, Different Meaning)
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the pronunciation of both words. Step 2: Understand their different meanings. Step 3: Choose the correct word according to the sentence context. Example: 'Their' (belonging to them), 'There' (place), 'They're' (they are).

sections.title: Single Filler Context Rule
sections.content: Step 1: Read the entire sentence carefully. Step 2: Understand the meaning from the words around the blank. Step 3: Choose the correct homophone according to the meaning. Example: 'She lost ___ keys.' The correct word is 'her', not 'here'.

sections.title: Common Homophone Groups
sections.content: Some common groups are: to/too/two, there/their/they're, your/you're, hear/here, break/brake, buy/by/bye. These words have different meanings, so choosing the correct one depends on the sentence context.

sections.title: Meaning Comparison Strategy
sections.content: To understand homophones, remember their meanings separately and observe how they are used in sentences. This helps reduce confusion.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Choosing a word only based on pronunciation. 2. Ignoring spelling differences. 3. Not reading the sentence context carefully.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Homophones sound the same but have different meanings and spellings. To choose the correct word, it is important to understand both the sentence context and the meaning of the words.

tricks.title: Context First Rule
tricks.explanation: First understand the meaning of the sentence.

tricks.title: They're = They Are
tricks.explanation: 'They're' is always the short form of 'they are'.

tricks.title: Your Possession Trick
tricks.example: Your bag is on the table.

tricks.title: Hear vs Here Trick
tricks.explanation: 'Hear' is related to listening, while 'Here' refers to a place.
tricks.example: I can hear music from here.
